title: Capacity forecast (Q1) — Top enterprise protected routes (Hosted API + Dedicated spillover)
content:
Context / why this exists
- The hot-route capacity protection work introduces tier-aware admission control and explicit enterprise budgets for a small set of high-SLA routes.
- Infra needs a Q1 GPU plan that matches the intended protection behavior: enterprise traffic must have headroom during overload; best-effort traffic will shed earlier.
- This sheet is the working forecast used for provider reservations + internal fleet allocation (hosted pools + dedicated spillover).

Owners / review
- Infra: Jamal Pierce (owner), Irene Choi (review)
- Fleet reporting: Vanessa Ortiz
- SRE constraints / load-shed assumptions: Rafael Mendes
- Routing/policy constraints: Mina Haddad, Ethan Park

Protected route set (MVP)
1) /v1/chat/completions (enterprise chat)
2) /v1/embeddings
3) /v1/rerank

Regions in scope for Q1
- us-east (primary)
- eu-west (secondary)
- us-west (burst / failover for select enterprise accounts)

Key assumptions (please read)
A. Growth + seasonality
- Enterprise traffic growth assumed: +18% MoM for chat, +12% MoM for embeddings, +10% MoM for rerank.
- Weekday peak-to-average ratio (PAR): chat 2.6x, embeddings 2.2x, rerank 1.8x.
- Planning target: provision for P95 weekday peak + 30% headroom (headroom supports SLO stability and failover).

B. Model mapping (current Q1 default profiles)
- Chat: Redwood Chat Large (70B-class), primarily H100 80GB (preferred) with a limited A100 fallback pool for non-strict accounts.
- Embeddings: Redwood Embeddings (large), L40S preferred (cost), with A100 for strict latency tenants in us-east.
- Rerank: Redwood Rerank (medium), L40S/A10 depending on region availability.

C. “Effective capacity” per GPU (used for rough sizing)
Note: this is not a microbenchmark; it’s an SRE-safe planning constant that bakes in prefill/decode mix, batching, and SLO constraints.
- H100 (chat profile): 2,200 effective tokens/sec/GPU at peak (prefill+decode combined) at p95 latency target.
- A100 (chat fallback profile): 1,350 effective tokens/sec/GPU at peak.
- L40S (embeddings profile): 35,000 embedding tokens/sec/GPU at peak.
- L40S/A10 (rerank profile): 7,500 rerank tokens/sec/GPU at peak.

D. Budgeting rule introduced by hot-route protection
- Enterprise class gets a reserved “protected budget” per route/region.
- Best-effort shares remaining headroom and is first to shed when queue depth/scheduler lag exceeds thresholds.
- For planning we assume enterprise consumes 65–80% of hot-route capacity at peak depending on route; we size enterprise budget to cover forecast + headroom (best-effort sits outside that budget).

E. Dedicated tier spillover
- A subset of Dedicated customers burst into hosted pools during planned maintenance windows and region failover drills.
- For Q1 we carry a 10% “spillover buffer” in us-east and 5% in eu-west on chat only.


Input summary (forecasted enterprise demand at peak)
Units:
- RPS = requests/sec
- tpr = tokens/request (prompt + completion), for embeddings this is input tokens
- tok/s = RPS * tpr
- GPUs = tok/s / effective_tok_per_sec_per_GPU

Forecast by route (enterprise only, weekday peak, aggregated across regions)
| Route | Jan peak RPS | Jan tpr | Jan tok/s | Feb peak RPS | Feb tpr | Feb tok/s | Mar peak RPS | Mar tpr | Mar tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| /v1/chat/completions | 520 | 2,200 | 1,144,000 | 614 | 2,250 | 1,381,500 | 724 | 2,300 | 1,665,200 |
| /v1/embeddings | 1,950 | 650 | 1,267,500 | 2,184 | 650 | 1,419,600 | 2,445 | 650 | 1,589,250 |
| /v1/rerank | 780 | 520 | 405,600 | 858 | 520 | 446,160 | 944 | 520 | 490,880 |

Notes on tpr
- Chat tpr trending up due to tool-calling + longer context in 2 enterprise tenants; we assume modest increase each month.
- Embeddings tpr stable (docs ingestion mix doesn’t change materially Q1).
- Rerank tpr stable.


Region split assumptions (enterprise only)
- Chat: us-east 58%, eu-west 27%, us-west 15%
- Embeddings: us-east 55%, eu-west 35%, us-west 10%
- Rerank: us-east 60%, eu-west 25%, us-west 15%


GPU requirement calculations (enterprise budget only; adds headroom + spillover)
Headroom policy applied: (forecast_tok/s * (1 + 0.30 headroom) * (1 + spillover_buffer))
- spillover_buffer: chat only (us-east 10%, eu-west 5%, us-west 0%); embeddings/rerank 0%.

A) Chat — H100 primary sizing (A100 fallback handled separately)
Mar (peak) enterprise tok/s by region
- us-east: 1,665,200 * 0.58 = 965,816 tok/s
- eu-west: 1,665,200 * 0.27 = 449,604 tok/s
- us-west: 1,665,200 * 0.15 = 249,780 tok/s

Mar protected-budget GPU needs (H100)
- us-east: 965,816 * 1.30 * 1.10 / 2,200 ≈ 628 H100
- eu-west: 449,604 * 1.30 * 1.05 / 2,200 ≈ 279 H100
- us-west: 249,780 * 1.30 * 1.00 / 2,200 ≈ 148 H100

Chat H100 total (Mar): ~1,055 H100 (enterprise protected budget)

Chat A100 fallback pool (for non-strict accounts + controlled fallback policies)
- Goal: cover up to 12% of chat protected budget during H100 maintenance / partial supply gaps in us-east only (routing guardrails prevent silent fallback for strict tenants).
- us-east A100 fallback target: 0.12 * 628 H100-equivalent capacity
- Convert capacity: H100 2,200 tok/s vs A100 1,350 tok/s => 1 H100 ≈ 1.63 A100
- A100 count: 0.12 * 628 * 1.63 ≈ 123 A100 (us-east)

B) Embeddings — L40S primary sizing
Mar embeddings tok/s by region
- us-east: 1,589,250 * 0.55 = 874,088 tok/s
- eu-west: 1,589,250 * 0.35 = 556,238 tok/s
- us-west: 1,589,250 * 0.10 = 158,925 tok/s

Mar protected-budget GPU needs (L40S @ 35,000 tok/s)
- us-east: 874,088 * 1.30 / 35,000 ≈ 33 L40S
- eu-west: 556,238 * 1.30 / 35,000 ≈ 21 L40S
- us-west: 158,925 * 1.30 / 35,000 ≈ 6 L40S

Embeddings L40S total (Mar): ~60 L40S

Embeddings strict-latency A100 carve-out (us-east)
- Assumption: 18% of embeddings enterprise traffic flagged strict (can’t move to L40S in peak hours without latency risk).
- us-east strict tok/s: 874,088 * 0.18 = 157,336 tok/s
- A100 required (using 35,000 tok/s equivalent is not accurate for embeddings on A100; use conservative 28,000 tok/s): 157,336 * 1.30 / 28,000 ≈ 8 A100

C) Rerank — L40S/A10 sizing
Mar rerank tok/s by region
- us-east: 490,880 * 0.60 = 294,528 tok/s
- eu-west: 490,880 * 0.25 = 122,720 tok/s
- us-west: 490,880 * 0.15 = 73,632 tok/s

Mar protected-budget GPU needs (rerank profile @ 7,500 tok/s)
- us-east: 294,528 * 1.30 / 7,500 ≈ 52 GPUs
- eu-west: 122,720 * 1.30 / 7,500 ≈ 22 GPUs
- us-west: 73,632 * 1.30 / 7,500 ≈ 13 GPUs

Rerank total (Mar): ~87 GPUs (L40S preferred; A10 acceptable in us-west where L40S supply is tighter)


Q1 purchase / reservation plan (by region)
Interpretation: these are the “protected enterprise budgets” we want guaranteed in each region by end of month, not total fleet size (best-effort pools are additive and can be opportunistic/spot).

| Region | Jan target | Feb target | Mar target | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| us-east H100 (chat) | 520 | 585 | 628 | Includes 10% spillover buffer. Priority routing depends on this being stable capacity. |
| eu-west H100 (chat) | 230 | 255 | 279 | Includes 5% spillover buffer. Watch EU provider lead times. |
| us-west H100 (chat) | 120 | 135 | 148 | No spillover buffer. Mainly failover + a handful of enterprise workloads. |
| us-east A100 (chat fallback) | 90 | 110 | 123 | Fallback only for non-strict tenants; requires guardrails + customer messaging alignment. |
| us-east L40S (embeddings) | 26 | 30 | 33 | Embeddings mostly cost-optimized. |
| eu-west L40S (embeddings) | 17 | 19 | 21 | |
| us-west L40S (embeddings) | 5 | 6 | 6 | |
| us-east A100 (embeddings strict carve-out) | 6 | 7 | 8 | Separate from chat fallback pool. |
| us-east rerank GPUs (L40S/A10) | 40 | 46 | 52 | Prefer L40S; allow A10 as needed. |
| eu-west rerank GPUs (L40S) | 18 | 20 | 22 | |
| us-west rerank GPUs (A10 ok) | 10 | 12 | 13 | |

Reserved vs on-demand assumptions (Q1)
- H100: 85–90% reserved, 10–15% on-demand/spot (spot only for best-effort pools; protected budgets should not be spot-backed).
- A100: 70% reserved, 30% on-demand (A100 supply is more flexible; still avoid relying on spot for fallback that might be needed during an incident).
- L40S/A10: 50–60% reserved, 40–50% on-demand (acceptable because embeddings/rerank can shed earlier for best-effort; enterprise budgets still need a stable core).

Provider plan (working, not final)
- us-east: lock H100 reservations first (largest risk); second priority is eu-west H100.
- eu-west: reserve early due to longer lead time + fewer available SKUs.
- us-west: keep smaller reserved footprint; fill gaps with on-demand in normal ops.


Risk notes / blockers (actionable)
1) H100 supply risk (high)
- Risk: provider cannot fulfill full Mar target in eu-west; us-east OK but might be delayed 2–4 weeks.
- Mitigation:
  - Pull forward reservation requests by 2 weeks.
  - Expand acceptable H100 host types (more instance families) if runtime compatibility is validated.
  - Keep A100 fallback pool warm in us-east with strict guardrails (no silent quality regressions).
- Owner: Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz

2) Cross-region failover increases instantaneous demand (medium)
- Risk: during a regional impairment, protected routes may shift traffic and temporarily exceed the destination region budget.
- Mitigation:
  - Ensure routing policy caps failover percentage per tenant (contract-dependent).
  - Pre-plan “failover drills” with explicit traffic caps and SRE approval.
  - Maintain headroom policy at 30% (do not shrink below 25% without SRE sign-off).
- Owner: Mina Haddad / Rafael Mendes

3) Model / token-shape drift (medium)
- Risk: chat token/request could jump >15% if customers increase context windows or enable new tool chains; GPU needs scale linearly.
- Mitigation:
  - Weekly review of token-per-request distributions for top enterprise tenants.
  - If tpr drift >10% WoW for 2 weeks, re-forecast and trigger expedited procurement.
- Owner: Vanessa Ortiz / Logan Wright (metrics), Jamal Pierce (capacity)

4) Over-reliance on on-demand for L40S (low/medium)
- Risk: embeddings cost profile could worsen if on-demand pricing spikes; also could reduce stability if supply tight.
- Mitigation:
  - Increase reserved L40S in us-east by +6 GPUs if provider pricing locks are favorable.
- Owner: Jamal Pierce

5) Non-GPU bottlenecks (often missed)
- Risk: even with GPUs, queue depth and tail latency can be driven by CPU, networking, or scheduler overhead during spikes.
- Mitigation:
  - Confirm gateway/routing fleet sizing matches Mar peak + headroom.
  - Validate autoscaling guardrails don’t throttle critical services during overload.
- Owner: Keiko Yamamoto / Ethan Park


Open questions
- Do we need a separate protected budget for “streaming chat” vs “non-streaming chat” given different tail behaviors? (SRE suggested yes; routing says keep it one route-group for now, revisit after GA metrics.)
- Confirm whether eu-west needs a larger spillover buffer due to smaller absolute fleet (currently 5%).
- Confirm which enterprise contracts require strict no-fallback (impacts sizing of A100 fallback usefulness).


Next steps
- 2026-01-28: finalize provider reservation requests for H100 (us-east + eu-west).
- 2026-02-04: re-forecast with post-canary data (queue depth + shed rates) and adjust headroom if needed.
- 2026-02-10: confirm us-west posture for failover drill; update spillover buffer.

Changelog
- 2026-01-24: updated chat tpr assumptions (+50 tokens Feb, +50 tokens Mar) based on top-3 enterprise tenant prompt growth; increased us-east spillover buffer to 10% per routing/SRE guidance.
- 2026-01-09: initial draft from Nov incident follow-ups + MVP protected routes list.
